items.title: Borel Equivariant Integration Conventions for the ABBV Formula
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ have the standard product presentation, smooth structure, and period-one basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of the upstream torus definition. Use its selected product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ with the right diagonal action and $BT=ET/T$. For a smooth left $T$-manifold $X$, define real Borel equivariant cohomology by $H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)=H^*(ET\times_T X;\mathbb R)$ using the quotient convention $(e\cdot t,x)\sim(e,t\cdot x)$. Its coefficient ring is $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)=\mathbb R[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i$ is the class corresponding to the dual period-one basis vector $e_i^*$ and each $u_i$ has degree $2$.

For an integer vector $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$, write the character as $\chi_m(t)=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i m_i t_i)$ and define its degree-two class by $u_{\chi_m}=\sum_i m_i u_i$. With the stated quotient convention, this is the Euler class of the Borel line $ET\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$, where $T$ acts on $\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$ by $\chi_m$. Use the complex-orientation convention $c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line $L$; thus $u_\chi$ is also the first Chern class of its Borel character line. Let $S\subset\mathcal R$ be the multiplicative set generated by these classes for all nontrivial characters, together with $1$; thus $u_\chi\ne0$ exactly for nontrivial $\chi$. Write $S^{-1}H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)$ and $S^{-1}\mathcal R$ for the corresponding localizations. The coefficient-ring identification is used under AC: the upstream classifying-space cohomology proof invokes AC in its Künneth and coefficient arguments.

If $X$ is a compact oriented smooth $T$-manifold without boundary of dimension $n$ and the action preserves its orientation, the Borel projection $\pi_X:ET\times_T X\to BT$ has compact oriented $n$-dimensional fibers. Define equivariant integration $\int_X\alpha=(\pi_X)_!\alpha$, the cohomological pushforward along those fibers; it lowers degree by $n$ and has values in $\mathcal R$. For an oriented $T$-equivariant vector bundle $E\to X$ whose Borel-associated bundle has a normalized Thom class, define its equivariant Euler class $e_T(E)$ as the pullback of that Thom class by the zero section. The Thom class is normalized to restrict on each oriented fiber pair $(D^c,S^{c-1})$ to the positive generator of $H^c(D^c,S^{c-1};\mathbb R)$. For rank $c=0$, the Thom class and Euler class are $1$. For a complex representation line of character $\chi$, this convention gives Euler class $u_\chi$. For a fixed component $F$ of a $T$-action on $M$, the orientation convention is $o(TM|_F)=o(TF)\wedge o(\nu_F)$, where $\nu_F$ is its chosen equivariantly oriented normal bundle. This is the Borel convention; no identification with a Cartan, Chow, or quotient-stack cohomology model is assumed here.

references.title: Michael F. Atiyah and Raoul Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
Matvei Libine, Lecture Notes on Equivariant Cohomology

items.title: Equivariant Thom-Gysin Identities for Fixed Submanifolds
items.statement:
Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T$ be a compact torus acting smoothly on a compact oriented smooth manifold $M$ without boundary. Let $N\subseteq M^T$ be a compact closed embedded submanifold without boundary of codimension $c$, let $i:N\hookrightarrow M$ be inclusion, and let its normal bundle $
u$ have a $T$-invariant orientation. Orient $N$ by $o(TM|_N)=o(TN)\wedge o(
u)$. If $N=\varnothing$, the source groups and all asserted maps are zero. Otherwise, with the real Borel conventions of the preceding definition, there is a fiber-normalized equivariant Thom class $	au_
u\in H_T^c(
u,
u\setminus N;\mathbb R)$, and cup product with $	au_
u$ is an isomorphism $H_T^k(N;\mathbb R)	o H_T^{k+c}(
u,
u\setminus N;\mathbb R)$ for every $k$. A $T$-invariant tubular neighborhood and excision therefore define a cohomological Gysin map $i_*^T:H_T^k(N;\mathbb R)	o H_T^{k+c}(M;\mathbb R)$. It satisfies

$$i^*i_*^T( eta)=e_T(
u)\smile eta,\qquad \int_M i_*^T( eta)=\int_N eta.$$

If $N'$ is a different fixed component disjoint from $N$, then $i_{N'}^*i_{N*}^T( eta)=0$. These maps use the Thom normalization in which every oriented normal fiber integrates to $1$.

Matvei Libine, Lecture Notes on Equivariant Cohomology
Kentaro Hori et al., Mirror Symmetry

items.title: Fixed-Component Normal Euler Classes Become Invertible
items.statement:
Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let a compact torus $T$ act smoothly on a compact smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, and let $F=M^T$. Then $F$ is a compact smooth embedded submanifold, its connected components $F_j$ are finite in number, and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$ for every $p\in F$. If $F=\varnothing$, the component assertions are vacuous. The normal bundle $
u_j$ of each component has no trivial $T$-representation in any fiber. Give $
u_j$ a $T$-equivariant orientation, write $c_j=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb R}
u_j$, and choose an invariant complex structure on it; let $\epsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$ compare that complex orientation with the chosen orientation. If the nonzero characters of the normal representation on a fiber, counted with multiplicity, are $\chi_{j,1},\ldots,\chi_{j,c_j/2}$, then the component of $e_T(
u_j)$ in $H^0(F_j;\mathbb R)\otimes\mathcal R$ is

$$\epsilon_j\prod_{a=1}^{c_j/2}u_{\chi_{j,a}}.$$

Consequently $e_T(
u_j)$ is invertible in $S^{-1}H_T^*(F_j;\mathbb R)$. When $c_j=0$, the product is empty, equals $1$, and the Euler class is already a unit.

references.title: Michael F. Atiyah and Raoul Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
Matvei Libine, Lecture Notes on Equivariant Cohomology
Kentaro Hori et al., Mirror Symmetry
references.locator: Chapter 4, §4.3, printed pp. 63–64 (PDF pp. 83–84), normal weights and denominator discussion.

items.title: Atiyah–Bott–Berline–Vergne Integration Formula
items.statement:
Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T$ be a compact torus acting smoothly on a compact oriented smooth $n$-manifold $M$ without boundary; use the standard Hausdorff, second-countable manifold convention, and assume the action preserves the orientation. Write $F=M^T=\coprod_{j=1}^{s}F_j$ for its fixed locus, with $s<\infty$, and $i_j:F_j\hookrightarrow M$ for each connected component. Give each normal bundle $\nu_j$ a $T$-equivariant orientation and orient $F_j$ by $o(TM|_{F_j})=o(TF_j)\wedge o(\nu_j)$. Use real Borel equivariant cohomology, $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)$, the multiplicative set $S$ generated by nonzero character classes, and the degree-shifting fiber-integration convention of the preceding definition. For every homogeneous $\alpha\in H_T^k(M;\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_M\alpha=\sum_j\int_{F_j}\frac{i_j^*\alpha}{e_T(\nu_j)}\quad\text{in }S^{-1}H^{k-n}(BT;\mathbb R).$$

If the fixed locus is isolated, use the ambient orientation on each normal space $\nu_p=T_pM$ and the positive orientation on each point $p$. Necessarily $n=2m$. Choose a $T$-invariant complex structure on each $T_pM$ and let $\chi_{p,1},\ldots,\chi_{p,m}$ be its nonzero character weights. Let $\epsilon_p=+1$ when its complex orientation agrees with the orientation of $M$ at $p$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then the same formula specializes to

$$\int_M\alpha=\sum_{p\in M^T}\frac{\epsilon_p\,i_p^*\alpha}{\prod_{a=1}^{m}u_{\chi_{p,a}}}\quad\text{in }S^{-1}\mathcal R.$$

This is a finite-dimensional formula for compact manifolds; it does not assert a formula for arbitrary noncompact instanton spaces or infinite-dimensional field spaces.

references.title: Michael F. Atiyah and Raoul Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
Matvei Libine, Lecture Notes on Equivariant Cohomology
Kentaro Hori et al., Mirror Symmetry
references.locator: Chapter 4, §4.3, printed pp. 62–64 (PDF pp. 82–84), equations (4.2)–(4.4) and the fixed-component pushforward derivation.

items.title: ABBV on the Projective Line with the Standard Circle Action
items.statement:
Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T=S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act on complex-oriented $M=\mathbb{CP}^1$ by $\lambda[z_0:z_1]=[z_0:\lambda z_1]$. Let $u\in H^2(BT;\mathbb R)$ be the class corresponding to the period-one weight-$+1$ character under the chosen tautological-Euler normalization, let $\mathcal O(1)$ be the dual tautological line with its induced equivariant structure, and put $x=e_T(\mathcal O(1))$. The fixed points are $p_0=[1:0]$ and $p_\infty=[0:1]$. Their tangent weights are $+1$ and $-1$, while $x|_{p_0}=0$ and $x|_{p_\infty}=-u$. The ABBV sum is

$$\frac{0}{u}+\frac{-u}{-u}=1,$$

which agrees with $\int_{\mathbb{CP}^1}x=1$.

references.title: Michael F. Atiyah and Raoul Bott, The Moment Map and Equivariant Cohomology
Matvei Libine, Lecture Notes on Equivariant Cohomology
Kentaro Hori et al., Mirror Symmetry
references.locator: Chapter 4, §4.3, printed pp. 62–64 (PDF pp. 82–84), fixed-point denominator context; the stated O(1) calculation is derived locally.

items.title: ABBV with Positive-Dimensional Fixed Components
items.statement: Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T=S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act on complex-oriented $M=\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$ by $\lambda([z_0:z_1],[w_0:w_1])=([z_0:\lambda z_1],[w_0:w_1])$. Let $\eta\in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1;\mathbb R)$ be the positive generator with integral $1$, let $x_1$ be the pullback of the equivariant Euler class of the dual tautological line from the first factor, and set $\alpha=x_1\smile\operatorname{pr}_2^*\eta$. The fixed components are $F_0=\{[1:0]\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1$ and $F_\infty=\{[0:1]\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1$, with normal weights $+1$ and $-1$. The component formula gives a zero contribution from $F_0$ and $\int_{\mathbb{CP}^1}\eta=1$ from $F_\infty$, matching $\int_M\alpha=1$.
